articles.title: Audi Q3 Launches in the UAE with “Beyond the Map” Discovery Experience
articles.desc:
Audi Q3 Launches in the UAE with “Beyond the Map” Discovery Experience

Audi and Al Nabooda Automobiles are celebrating the arrival of the all-new Audi Q3 with Beyond the Map, a unique initiative inviting residents to discover hidden gems and local destinations across the UAE.

Dubai, UAE – 27 October 2026 – Audi, in partnership with Al Nabooda Automobiles, has introduced Beyond the Map , a discovery initiative celebrating the launch of the all-new Audi Q3. The project brings together automotive innovation, local culture and exploration, encouraging residents to venture beyond the UAE’s well-known landmarks and discover lesser-known destinations.

At the heart of the initiative is a curated discovery guide featuring 30 destinations across the UAE. The collection includes independent cafés, family-run restaurants, local farms, cultural experiences and unique accommodation options, highlighting the people, traditions and stories that contribute to the country’s diverse identity.

The initiative also includes exclusive Audi Q3 driving experiences, taking participants to selected destinations such as Juntas, a family-run bakery located in an Emirati home; Houd, a restaurant celebrating traditional Emirati cuisine; and Guernsey Dairy, a family-operated farm in Al Ain.

In addition to the private driving experiences, these three destinations will host public Audi pop-up activations from 27 October to 9 November 2026 , giving visitors an opportunity to experience the new Audi Q3 while exploring some of the UAE’s local attractions.

Through Beyond the Map, Audi is positioning the all-new Q3 as more than just a new vehicle launch, connecting the driving experience with discovery, local businesses and the diverse destinations that make the UAE unique.

articles.title: Vehicle Report Turns One: Disrupting Used Car Buying for Over 42,000 UAE Drivers and Counting
articles.desc:
A year ago, purchasing a used car in the GCC often meant navigating limited information and a lack of transparency. In response, AutoData Middle East launched Vehicle Report – an AI-powered platform designed to place greater control in the hands of consumers. Over the past 12 months, more than 42,000 users have turned to the service to access verified data on ownership, accident history, valuation, and more. Daily usage has tripled between July 2024 and March 2025, with over 5,000 users now engaging each month. Of those, 84% reported no post-purchase issues, underscoring the platform’s role in reducing buyer risk and building confidence through accurate, accessible insight.

Empowering Informed, Efficient Car Buying

Vehicle Report stands out by turning fragmented automotive data into clear, actionable insight. Built around real consumer needs, the platform supports smarter, safer, and faster decision-making throughout the used car journey, before committing:

Save Money: Compare loan and insurance offers side by side, with market-aligned valuations to avoid overpaying.

Buy Smart: Access a car’s full history, including accidents and ownership lineage, maintenance data, pre-purchase inspection insights and service records, with a single Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) lookup.

Save Time: Instantly aggregating listings, while filtering and forecasting in real-time from multiple sales portals, streamlining the car-buying process.

Through this consolidated approach, the platform is shifting the regional automotive experience from reactive to data-driven, bridging the gap between information and confident decision-making for today’s car buyers.

As the UAE’s used car market continues to grow, residual value performance remains a crucial indicator of vehicle quality and long-term value. In Q2 2025, data from AutoData shows that family-friendly vehicles such as the Kia Carens LX continue to hold strong residual value (78% after 3 years), thanks to a balance of affordability, spacious design, and efficient ownership costs. Within the SUV category, the Toyota Land Cruiser GXR was recognised as the best-value model (81% after 3 years), combining robust specification levels with competitive market pricing and favourable depreciation profiles.

As Vehicle Report continues to gain momentum across the region, AutoData Middle East is expanding its suite of tools to support smarter decisions for both consumers and industry partners.

Among its upcoming innovations is an AI-powered pricing engine that delivers real-time car valuations using over 100 million data points – factoring in market trends, specs, and condition to reveal a vehicle’s true worth, whether buying, selling or trading in.

Also in development is Claim Hub , a tool for insurers to detect total loss vehicles, reduce fraud, and accelerate claims – enhancing accountability across the ecosystem and building long-term trust for buyers.

With a future-ready focus, AutoData is bridging data and trust to make car ownership safer, simpler, and smarter.

“Our mission has always been to bring clarity and confidence to the automotive ecosystem,” said Sebastian Fuchs, Managing Director of AutoData Middle East. “With advanced AI at its core, Vehicle Report delivers real-time, market-specific pricing and risk analysis – helping buyers save up to 25% on average. More than a history check, it’s a decision-making engine that unifies pricing, ownership, and insurance data to transform how used cars are bought and sold. As we grow, we’re focused on deeper integrations with insurers, banks, and marketplaces, and on launching tools like AutoMagic and Claim Hub to further streamline the process. We’re proud to be raising the bar for transparency and intelligence in automotive transactions.”

With AI-powered technology, trust, and transparency at its core, Vehicle Report is redefining how the UAE buys and sells used cars. Now entering its second year, it’s more than just a report – it’s a smart ecosystem built to empower better decisions, from valuation to insurance to ownership.

articles.title: Range Rover Evoque and Velar Are Being Discontinued: What It Means for Buyers in the UAE
articles.desc:
Range Rover is about to become a lot more exclusive. Jaguar Land Rover has confirmed that the Evoque and Velar, the two cheapest Range Rovers, will be discontinued during 2027 with no direct replacements. For many UAE drivers, those two cars were the way into the Range Rover brand. Here is what is changing, what replaces them, and what it means if you are thinking of buying one.

Evoque and Velar production ends during 2027, with no new generations planned

The all-electric Range Rover GT arrives in 2027 as the new entry point, at a much higher price

Range Rover’s lineup shrinks to three models: Range Rover, Range Rover Sport and the GT

Defender and Discovery will cover the more affordable end of JLR’s range

No UAE-specific announcement on the GT or final Evoque and Velar orders yet

Range Rover’s managing director, Martin Limpert, told Autocar that neither a third-generation Evoque nor a second-generation Velar is in development. JLR has since confirmed that both models will stay on sale in selected global markets where demand remains strong throughout 2027, with production ending as its factories switch to building new vehicles. Reports differ on whether production stops in mid-2027 or by year-end, so the exact date is not clear. The Discovery Sport is also reported to end production this year.

The change is part of JLR’s “House of Brands” strategy, which has split Land Rover into three separate brands: Range Rover, Defender and Discovery. Range Rover is being pushed towards a smaller, more exclusive range, while Defender and Discovery will take over the volume end of the market that the Evoque and Velar served. The soon-to-be-unveiled Defender Sport is reported to become the company’s entry-level model.

The Range Rover GT was revealed in July as the brand’s fifth model. It is a low, coupe-like electric grand tourer, and Range Rover calls it the most car-like model it has ever built. Key facts so far:

It is the first model on JLR’s new Electrified Modular Architecture (EMA), electric first, with a hybrid to follow later

All-wheel drive at launch, built at the Halewood plant in the UK

Production is due in the first half of 2027

Battery size, range and power figures have not been announced

JLR says the GT is not a direct Velar replacement. It will cost much more: estimates range from about £90,000 to £100,000 (roughly AED 436,000 to AED 485,000 / US$118,800 to US$132,000, at approximate exchange rates). Range Rover has not confirmed any price, and there is no UAE pricing or launch date yet.

What Do the Evoque and Velar Cost in the UAE?

UAE prices vary by listing site and specification. Third-party listings show the 2026 Evoque starting from about AED 185,000 (US$50,374), and the 2026 Velar from about AED 277,600 (US$75,590), rising to about AED 460,000 (US$125,255) for the top Autobiography version. Treat these as indicative and ask the dealer for current prices and any year-end offers.

Thinking of buying one? Ask your dealer how long new Evoque and Velar orders will be accepted in the UAE, because JLR has only said they will continue in selected markets.

Ask about support: check how long parts and service will be available for discontinued models and what the warranty covers.

Waiting for the GT? It is a different, more expensive car, and there is no UAE price or date yet.

On a smaller budget? Look at the Defender and Discovery line-up as JLR’s more accessible options.

The Evoque and Velar helped bring a whole new group of buyers into the Range Rover brand. With them gone, getting into a Range Rover will cost a lot more. Do you think this is the right move? Tell us in the comments.

articles.desc:
The new BendPak PL-12000KDS and PL-12000KDT double-wide parking lifts securely store four vehicles in two parking spots without the hassle associated with traditional double-wide parking lifts. Plus, their narrow footprint allows more lifts to fit in a facility.

The PL-12000KDS/KDT models are the latest in the PL-12000 tandem lift lineup and feature BendPak’s patent-pending independent platform design. Traditional double-wide parking lifts require all vehicles on the bottom to be removed before those on top can be lowered. The PL-12000 series platforms operate independently, so one can be lowered while the other remains stationary. Only one vehicle must be moved to access a vehicle parked above. The platform architecture provides double-car-width open front access to improve entry and exit efficiency.

With commercial and residential development costs rising, maximizing vehicle capacity within existing space can deliver cost savings.

“Our new PL-12000KDS and PL-12000KDT tandem parking lifts feature a narrower footprint than our original PL-12000 models for customers who want to maximize the number of lifts they can fit in their parking facility,” said Jeff Kritzer, president and CEO of BendPak. “Reducing the width by 15.5 inches, from 221.5 to 206 inches, allows more vehicles to be stored in a facility without expanding the building space. When filling a warehouse, saving just a few inches per lift means 20 lifts can be installed instead of 19 or fewer — that’s space to accommodate at least four more cars.”

The PL-12000KDS offers a standard max rise of 70 inches and short platforms, while the PL-12000KDT has an extended rise of 82 inches and long platforms. articles.desc:
The pendulum is swinging, and major corporations with deep pockets are discussing the skilled workforce shortage, but that also means competition for a seat at the table will intensify, Jennifer Maher, TechForce Foundation CEO, told Repairer Driven News.

​“I worry that I don’t hear that same momentum in the collision industry,” Maher said.

​The U.S.Bureau of Labor has identified 47 different technician jobs using its standard occupational classification (SOC) system, Maher said. She said this includes everything from wind turbine techs to elevator technicians.

​“We’re all competing for the same person,” Maher said. “The person who is curious, likes to problem solve, takes it apart and puts it back together, gets a thrill out of making things work.”

​The collision industry competes with all of these different technician sectors, she said. The industry is also competing with all of the skilled trades, which include electricians, construction workers and plumbers.

​“You can’t just look at how to build collision techs in the collision program,” Maher said. “You have to cast your net really wide. We’re competing with all of those sectors.”

​Technicians are often overlooked in the conversation, she added.

​“I call them our hidden heroes because we all need technicians and we need to recognize and start talking about the importance of those service and maintenance technicians,” Maher said.

​As the pendulum swings, the conversation is heavily focused on construction jobs.

“I appreciate the need to bring back manufacturing and build more plants, build more housing, and build more data centers. That’s exciting and great, but in my world, I’m asking how do we keep what we have moving?”

​If technicians get lost in the conversation, then people will find themselves waiting on the tarmac because of a shortage of airplane technicians or waiting two months for their vehicle to be repaired because of a shortage of auto technicians, she said.

​“Techs are important and we need to be at the table,” Maher said. “That’s the bottom line, technicians need to be in the headlines and they need to be part of the excitement around the skilled trades.”

​The top 10 technician fields identified by the U.S. Bureau of Labor adds up to a workforce of 7 million people, she said.

​“Collectively they are a huge force but they are buried, hidden and not talked about,” Maher said.

​Even under the Bureau of Labor’s classification system, technicians are scattered throughout different industries including transportation, energy, industrial manufacturing and construction, she added.

​TechForce’s “Technician Supply, Demand & Opportunity Report.” found the U.S. economy is short roughly 140,000 skilled technicians a year, and the gap is widening, with 73,354 new collision repair entrant technicians needed by 2029 .

​It found that the collision repair sector sees the highest turnover of the 10 analyzed at 60.7%.

​Maher said TechForce Foundation continuously polls its 125,000 aspiring working techs to see which industries excite them.

​“I am worried about the collision industry because it does not resonate above the fold,” Maher said. “It is way down, way down on the list.”

​That is going to be a recruiting challenge for the collision industry, she adds.

articles.desc:
This year’s MSO Symposium brought together “the Four Aces” — the CEOs of Boyd Group, Caliber, Classic Collision, and Crash Champions —in Las Vegas on Monday, who ultimately landed on a simple conclusion: the collision repair industry depends on the right people fitting into the right roles.

When moderator Dan Risley asked what they’re hearing from investors and other stakeholders about the industry today, Boyd Group CEO Brian Kaner responded that the industry isn’t “recession-proof, but it is recession-resilient.”

“There are plenty of opportunities for us to continue to grow our businesses,” he said. “It all comes down to making sure you have the right people in the right roles with the right capabilities. And if you have that and you know how to keep score and you can win with the insurance carriers and you can take care of their customers and really be the extension of what they’re looking for, this is a great business to be in, and it’s something that we can continue to all thrive in.”

However, in response to a different question Risley posed about the “temperature” of each MSO’s team leaders, Crash Champions CEO Matt Ebert and Kaner agreed it’s a tense, stressful time for them, and made some important points about estimators.

Ebert said being an estimator, or as Crash Champions calls them, a service advisor, “has to be one of the most miserable spots.”

“You’ve got technicians bitching at you, you’ve got management or ownership bitching at you, you’ve got insurance companies bitching at you,” he said. “Everything you do gets criticized. Everything you do gets reviewed and sent back, and you have to do it again. I wouldn’t last a week. I would quit that job and tell you to shove it up your a**. If you want to know the temperature of our people, that is the truth.”

Ebert added that general managers also face pressure to keep customers, employees, and insurance companies happy while trying to make money and handle the safety, legal, and logistical pieces of their jobs.

Kaner said the industry has a “compelling opportunity” to invest in people.

“You’ve got to make investments in estimators,” he said. “We all make investments in technicians. I think one of the bigger gaps we have as an industry right now is in estimators. There’s not enough of them. There’s not enough of them that understand the metrics. There’s not enough of them that are salespeople that can go help actually go sell a consumer-paid job. …it’s a tense time and anytime when you’re in an environment where volume is tight, it just ups the pressure of the organization.”

Brad Anderson, who joined the collision repair industry in June to take over as CEO of Classic Collision, said he believes all jobs in the industry are hard.

“We put a lot on them, and I think all of us as an industry and ecosystem have to consider that it all crashes down to the people at the shop,” he said. “The small changes we make up here get really big when there’s 20 changes happening to the individual, whether it’s a tech, a GM, a service advisor, so we’ve got to simplify the work.”

During the discussion, Ebert also noted that 40-50% of MSO employees don’t touch a car, which he said “presents huge administrative opportunity,” another point he and Kaner agreed on.

“We have 15,000 people in our organization, and half of them are technicians and the other half are the people that are just trying to get the car to the back and do all the administrative things that they need to do to get it there,” Kaner said.

articles.title: Autel software update gains access to Nissan’s restricted CONSULT 4 vehicle line
articles.desc:
Nissan’s CONSULT 4 vehicle line secures access to critical vehicle systems, but Autel says it has gained access for ADAS calibrations and other services.

The software gives access to protected vehicle functions through AutoAuth, the release adds.

Marshall said this access is necessary to calibrate some 2025 and 2026 Nissan vehicles.

“We worked with Nissan U.S. and Japan to validate our process,” Marshall said.

The Equipment and Tool Institute (ETI) manages Autel’s Nissan licensing, Marshall further explained. He said ETI worked directly with Nissan during the process.

Allison A. Whitney, Autel’s director of corporate communications, told RDN that Nissan provided security-access information and reviewed diagnostic logs supplied by Autel. She adds that the automaker also provided guidance on accessing protected vehicle control modules and that in specific logs, Nissan confirmed successful security access and command transmission.

Whitney noted that “technical assistance is distinct from Nissan’s endorsement or certification of Autel products.”

Nissan’s technical review of particular access sequences and diagnostic logs should not be interpreted as product-wide validation, Whitney said.

“Approval for a dealer equipment program is also a separate matter,” Whitney said.

She adds that Autel is pursuing approval for its IA1000 through that process and approval is pending.

Autel’s diagnostic software for Nissan is available on MaxiSYS Ultra and Ultra S2 tablets, Autel’s release states. The ADAS calibration capabilities are available on Ultra and Ultra S2 series tablets with ADAS calibration software.

“On newer Nissan platforms, security-gateway restrictions previously prevented aftermarket diagnostic tools from accessing certain protected functions, including code clearing, Active Tests, and ADAS calibration procedures,” said Vinie Putrino, Autel senior testing specialist, during a live demonstration at Auto Glass Week 2026, according to the release. “This expanded access gives Autel users the ability to perform supported diagnostic and calibration functions through the established AutoAuth authorization process.”

The release notes that Nissan began incorporating security-gateway protections into select North American vehicles with the 2020 model year. The protections restrict access to designated bidirectional functions unless the technician, shop, and diagnostic tool are properly authenticated.

Autel has offered AutoAuth-based Nissan security-gateway access for several years on applicable vehicles supported by Nissan’s CONSULT-III plus diagnostic platform, according to the release.

CONSULT 4, Nissan’s newer web-based diagnostic software, was introduced for the 2023 Nissan Ariya and is now on a growing number of newer Nissan vehicle platforms, the release states. “Gateway access and access to a particular protected control module can involve separate requirements,” Whitney said. “Successful authentication does not, by itself, establish that every function is supported or that a calibration has been completed successfully.”

Autel-developed software communicates with the vehicle’s control modules to request supported diagnostic and service functions, Whitney explained. She said that the announced functionality does not run Nissan’s CONSULT 4.

Whitney describes the access as the breadth of supported bidirectional functions beyond reading fault codes and live data.

“Bidirectional capability allows the tool to send commands to the vehicle — for example, to activate a component for testing or initiate a supported ADAS calibration routine,” Whitney said. “Coverage varies by vehicle, control module, and procedure. U.S. Rep. Mike Lawler (R-NY-District 17) has filed a bill that would require auto dealerships and other resale channels selling used vehicles to sell them with functional airbag systems, or, if an airbag is missing or disabled, to clearly disclose that.

If passed, the bill would mean up to life in prison for sellers if someone dies as a result of a vehicle sold at an auction or dealership without disclosing the vehicle is missing an airbag or is equipped with a disabled one.

Lawler filed the Anthony Amoros Law Right to Know Act this week, according to a press release from his office .

Anthony Amoros died in 2013 at the age of 18 after crashing his car on a windy stretch of road, according to a New York CBS News report . Amoros’s family purchased the vehicle without knowing it lacked an airbag.

New York Gov. Kathy Hochul signed a bill titled “Anthony Amoros Law” in 2021 that prohibits used car dealers from selling vehicles without a working airbag, according to Spectrum News . The law requires sellers to provide consumers with certification that the vehicle is equipped with an airbag.

“Every driver and passenger deserves to know that the vehicle they are getting into is safe, and this bill will help protect consumers by making sure they have the information they need to make informed decisions,” Lawler said in his press release. “This legislation will ensure dealerships and third-party sellers cannot sell these vehicles without clearly informing consumers of the safety risks.”

Lawler’s bill would require sellers to disclose that vehicles don’t have a working airbag on the front of the sales contract receipt and invoice.

The proposed law would give state officials or agencies authority to regulate and enforce compliance after Federal Trade Commission (FTC) notice.

The FTC will have the right to intervene in any action or file a petition of appeal.

Penalties outlined in the bill allow for a court to award an additional $25,000 for an action that involves death or paralysis.

The bill states that those who knowingly sell a vehicle without a working airbag and disclosure could be fined and face up to 10 years in prison.

It adds that a seller could face up to 20 years in prison if someone is seriously injured, including paralysis.

The bill also defines a “deficiency” as a vehicle without a functional airbag system and/or inflatable restraint system.

Counterfeit airbags are not specifically mentioned in the bill. However, it’s likely that vehicles without an airbag or a deficient airbag system travel through the same salvage routes as vehicles with counterfeit airbags.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) recently identified an 11th death caused by a counterfeit airbag part that the agency banned earlier this year .

The death happened Aug. 27 in Dallas, Texas, and is described as an otherwise survivable crash by NHTSA.

The 2004-2013 Mazda 3 is based on the Ford global C1 platform, shared with the European Ford Focus and Volvo S40. Nothing is really groundbreaking about the mechanical brake system, but not paying attention to the details can end in a post-brake-job comeback.

A key service issue concerns the hydraulics and ABS system. The older the car, the greater the chance the brake fluid has not been serviced. Over time this can cause issues with the ABS hydraulic control unit.

For almost 10 years, Mazda used the same caliper, pad and rotor design. Pads should be replaced when there is 2mm or less of friction material. If the rotors are any thicker, they have enough material on them to last at least one turning on the lathe. The runout specification for these vehicles is .002” and disc thickness variation should be far below .0005”.

Mazda claims repeated panic braking may raise the temperature in some portions of the disc plate by approx. 1,000°C (l,832°F). This temperature is almost near impossible to achieve this side of a high-speed police chase.

All Mazda3 models have rear disc brakes. The calipers mount to the brackets using caliper guide pins with Allen heads. The sleeves and boots should be disassembled, cleaned and lubricated every time the brakes are replaced. The torque for the guide pins is 21 ft./lbs. and the caliper bracket bolts should be tightened to 55 ft./lbs.

Mazda uses a hand brake that is incorporated into the rear caliper, and a couple of systems are employed to retract rear pistons. The later-model cars require the familiar method of turning the piston clockwise while applying pressure, where others will have a plug on the back side of the caliper that provides access for an Allen wrench to facilitate retracting the piston. Remove the service hole cover of the rear console.

Turn the adjusting nut and adjust the parking brake lever.

After adjustment, pull the parking brake lever one notch and verify that the parking brake warning light illuminates and the rear brakes do not drag.

The Mazda3 comes in two styles, ABS and ABS with Dynamic Stability Control (DSC). Both systems connect to other vehicle components via a high-speed serial data bus. The DSC system ties more components together (like a yaw/pitch sensor and steering position sensor) onto the bus.

If you are seeing communication-related DTCs, it is essential that you fully diagnose problems with the system before you start replacing sensors and modules. Some of these vehicles have been on the road for more than six years and the connections will be starting to corrode and fret.

One of the main facilitators of ABS/DCS problems are the connectors, especially under the hood where the control/modulator unit connects. Being able to measure values at the connectors and observe data on a scan tool is essential for diagnosing problems.

articles.title: Volkswagen-Electronic-Parking-Brake
articles.desc:
The majority of Volkswagen vehicles sold in the past decade have electronic parking brakes. However, most customers don’t even realize that the vehicle has an electronic parking brake, because the system engages and disengages the parking brake automatically on most vehicles. But, when the system fails and turns on the light or has a warning in the driver information center, then the customer will notice.

If you are doing a brake job on a vehicle with an electronic parking brake, you will need a scan tool with the proper software for the parking brake system to retract the calipers, adjust and perform diagnostics. There are no shortcuts on YouTube. You can find videos that involve removing the electric motor, jumping connectors and disassembling the parking brake mechanism. But, these methods are very risky and can damage the vehicle and kill productivity. Unapproved methods will set malfunction codes, and the worst-case scenario is that you could damage the unit.

The VW system that was installed on many of its platforms starting in 2004 is an example of a system that requires a scan tool to replace the rear brake pads.

The system has stepper motors on the back of the caliper that actuate the piston. The motor can be removed from the caliper, though the ignition should be switched off for at least 30 seconds before removing the connector.

The motor is sealed to the caliper with an o-ring around the spindle. The condition of this o-ring is critical for the life of the motor and should be lightly lubricated with brake fluid. If the o-ring fails, water and debris will be one step closer to the motor gears.

The spindle on the caliper can be rocked slightly with a torx bit so the motor seats in the spindle. Don’t force the motor assembly onto the caliper, because damage to the housing can occur.

On recent platforms, VW have outfitted the motors with a sensor that can measure brake pad wear and adjust the pads for the least amount of drag. During this adjustment on some vehicles, the pad thickness is calculated. The system counts the number of rotations of the motor with a hall effect sensor inside the unit.

Inspecting the caliper, hardware and motors may not give you a complete picture of what is happening with these systems. Having access to a scan tool can reduce diagnostic time.

The OEMs have built-in bi-directional protocols to retract the parking brake so the pads can be replaced. A dedicated brake tool or enhanced scan tool is able to command these protocols and interrogate the module for codes and faults.

The Electronic Parking Brake Module (EPBM) is the module on the CAN bus of most vehicles equipped with this system. Any missing data for vehicle speed, gear position or brake pedal input will cause a problem with the system.

Some systems use information from the electric parking brake to track shoe and pad wear. The system will count the number of turns the actuator makes or the position of the stepper motor to determine the thickness of the friction material.

If you do find yourself working on a vehicle whose electronic parking brake will not disengage, the first thing to do is look at the basics. Some systems require that the doors be shut and the brake pedal depressed. Some models may even require the seat belt to be buckled. Simple items like a defective brake pedal or door switch may hinder operation. Also, in some cases, the button may be defective. On some vehicles, the operation of the switch can be verified with a scan tool.

articles.title: How Brake-Based Traction Control Helps AWD
articles.desc:
Many all-wheel-drive (AWD) systems reached the market during the 1990s, as the SUV boom gave automakers an opportunity to sell profitable light trucks. Many early SUVs used transfer cases, limited-slip or locking differentials, and locking hubs adapted from the automakers’ truck platforms. As buyers began asking for four-wheel-drive capability in smaller, more fuel-efficient vehicles, automakers developed lighter AWD systems for passenger cars and crossovers.

- Diagnosing Hub Units and Wheel Speed Sensor Air Gap Issues

Sending power to all four wheels is possible with either a longitudinal or transverse engine. A transverse layout can send power from the transaxle through a power takeoff unit and driveshaft to the rear axle. Depending on the design, the system may use a center differential, a coupling, or another device to manage the front-to-rear torque distribution. One feature these systems may lack, compared with traditional four-wheel-drive hardware, is a mechanical differential lock or limited-slip differential.

Engineers found another way to improve traction: use the ABS hardware to apply a brake at a slipping wheel. This brake-based traction control can make an open differential behave somewhat like a limited-slip differential in low-traction conditions.

An open differential allows the drive wheels to turn at different speeds while cornering. The ring gear turns the differential case, which carries small spider gears. Those gears mesh with side gears connected to the axle shafts. An open differential delivers similar torque to both axle shafts, but the torque available is limited by the wheel with less grip. If one tire is on a slippery surface, it can spin while the other tire receives too little torque to move the vehicle effectively.

Brake-based traction control addresses this by applying the brake at the spinning wheel. The added resistance creates a reaction torque through the differential, allowing more usable torque to reach the wheel with better grip. The system does not lock the differential mechanically, but it can produce a limited-slip effect. Some AWD systems also use brake control to manage wheelspin across the front and rear axles; the exact strategy depends on the vehicle’s driveline and control system.

The system makes quick adjustments based on wheel-speed signals. Depending on the vehicle, it may apply the brakes, reduce engine torque, or use both strategies to control wheelspin. Some drivers may feel or hear the brakes operating during a traction event. On some vehicles, limited brake-based traction functions remain active even when the driver switches off part of the stability-control system.

Brake-based traction control has limits compared with a four-wheel-drive system equipped with mechanically locking differentials. Brake application creates heat, and traction may be reduced if the system reaches its operating limits. Still, for drivers who encounter snow, mud, or other slippery conditions occasionally, the system can make a substantial difference.

These systems do not have differential clutches that require service, but brake-based traction control adds activity to the brakes and ABS hydraulic control unit. Follow the manufacturer’s brake-fluid specification and service interval. Some vehicles require a low-viscosity DOT 4 fluid so the hydraulic system can respond as designed; use it only when specified for that application.

Replacement brake pads should perform similarly to the original pads across the operating temperature range. A pad with different friction behavior may affect braking response and the system’s ability to control wheelspin.

Wheel-speed sensors are another service consideration. If a sensor or its circuit provides an inaccurate signal, the system may limit its operation or disable traction-control functions. That can reduce the vehicle’s ability to manage wheelspin in snow, mud or ice. Check for ABS and traction-control codes, inspect the sensor wiring and tone or encoder rings, and verify wheel-speed data before condemning a sensor.

articles.title: The Effect of Thin Brake Fluid on Vehicle Systems
articles.desc:
Lower-viscosity brake fluid plays a growing role in modern brake systems. Today’s vehicles require brake fluid to move quickly through hydraulic control units that support ABS, stability control, traction control and several ADAS braking functions.

- Dipstick Replacement Sensors: How They Work

- Don’t Forget Lubrication During an Oil Change

- Magnaflow President Dan Paolone on the ‘Long-Term Play’

Modern brake systems use faster valves, tighter internal passages and more frequent automatic brake interventions than systems used 20 years ago.

As a result, many late-model vehicles require lower-viscosity brake fluid. The goal is to maintain efficient fluid movement at low temperatures so the hydraulic unit can build and release pressure quickly.

Lower-Viscosity Brake Fluid Supports Faster Response

The ABS hydraulic unit is used, not only during panic stops, but for electronic stability control, traction control, adaptive cruise control, collision mitigation braking and automatic emergency braking.

Inside the hydraulic control unit, brake fluid moves through small valves and narrow passages. Lower viscosity allows pressure to increase and decrease faster, helping the system make quicker and more precise braking corrections.

Brake fluid condition is also important. Moisture contamination can increase viscosity, lower the boiling point and raise corrosion risk.

Technicians should use the exact brake fluid specified by the vehicle manufacturer and replace it according to the proper service information.

articles.title: Schaeffler Offers Aftermarket Parts for Toyota, Ford Hybrids
articles.desc:
The Schaeffler division is making two Vitesco repair solutions available to the automotive aftermarket: a Voltage Stabilization System (VSS) for micro hybrid vehicles from Toyota and Peugeot S.A. (PSA), and a 48V DC/DC converter for Ford mild hybrid vehicles.

- Preventing EV Lithium-ion Battery Fires

- Charging and Replacing Batteries with Advanced Power Management Systems

The VSS is available immediately. According to Schaeffler, it prevents voltage drops that can occur during automatic start-stop operation in micro-hybrid vehicles. The system consists of an Energy Storage System (ESS) with high-performance capacitors and a Power Electronics Unit (PEU).

Schaeffler notes that during the engine start process, the capacitors release energy stored while driving within a very short time, compensating for the high-power demand. Starting the engine via a starter-generator requires a comparatively high amount of energy.

If this energy is drawn solely from the conventional 12-volt electrical system, the voltage can briefly drop by several volts, causing visible flickering of the vehicle’s lighting and electronic displays. Schaeffler said that by stabilizing the voltage supply, the capacitors ensure smooth engine restarting and contribute to longer battery life, improved driving comfort and compliance with current emissions standards.

The Schaeffler Vitesco 48V DC/DC converter, available in May, is used in mild-hybrid vehicles equipped with a 48V starter generator and an additional battery to enable more efficient power delivery and boost performance during acceleration, the company says. The converter links the vehicle’s 48-volt electrical system with the 12-volt onboard electronics.

The converter is a component of energy management in mild-hybrid vehicles and for achieving type-approval compliant CO2 emissions. Its bidirectional design allows 12-volt components to be supplied from the 48-volt network while charging the starter battery. Conversely, in the event of a temporary failure, the 48-volt system can also draw energy from the 12-volt network, the company notes.

articles.desc:
A parking brake cable may be the part the technician calls for, but it may not be the only part the job needs. A few targeted questions at the counter can uncover related components, service requirements and wear items. That will give counter pros the opportunity to build a more complete order and help the shop finish the repair with one delivery.

- Autologue’s eCounterman Brings AI to Parts Sales

- AI Technology Brings New Capabilities to Parts Stores

- Counter Culture: Simplifying Belt Drive Repairs

When diagnosing parking brake issues, the technician may need to inspect cables and related parts for wear, rust and corrosion; clean, replace or lubricate components; adjust the assembly; and verify operation. Electronic parking brakes add caliper-piston retraction and integrated-caliper adjustment requirements.

When a tech asks for a parking brake cable, first ask: What’s the vehicle, and is the concern a broken cable, excessive travel, inadequate holding or a parking brake that won’t release? Ask whether the technician has inspected the associated hardware for corrosion, wear,or binding. If it’s an integrated parking brake, ask whether the caliper requires a specific retraction or adjustment procedure. For electronic systems, ask whether there are indicator-light or wiring concerns.

Use those answers to build a complete order. If cables or mechanical components are being replaced, ask whether the technician has inspected the remaining parking-brake components and whether cleaning or lubrication is required. On drum-type applications, ask whether the shoes, springs, pins, self-adjusters, levers, clips, and related hardware have been inspected.

On disc applications, related caliper components and attaching hardware may also require inspection or replacement. And always remind the technician that adjustment and electronic caliper procedures must follow manufacturer recommendations.

The round will support the industrialization and market introduction of Sonexos’ novel plasma-based technology for active noise control.Sonexos is developing a new way to tackle one of acoustics’ persistent engineering challenges: low-frequency noise from fans, compressors and motors. Conventional solutions typically require significant space and material and can restrict airflow. Sonexos instead uses an electronically controlled layer of plasma to absorb sound, creating a thin, lightweight solution with no moving parts.Deep tech with industrial relevance and societal impactFor Bosch Ventures, Sonexos brings together differentiated deep technology, industrial relevance and the potential to improve everyday life, a strong expression of Bosch’s “Invented for life” principle.“Technology is most valuable when it moves out of the laboratory and solves problems people experience every day. Sonexos is a strong example of that principle: outstanding deep tech addressing a very tangible challenge, with applications ranging from the appliances in our homes to the infrastructure powering the digital economy,” says Dr. Ingo Ramesohl, Managing Director of Bosch Ventures. “What convinced us in particular is the credible pathway toward industrial scale.” Swiss Technology for global MarketsSonexos’ technology originated in research at EPFL and combines plasma physics, high-voltage electronics and adaptive control software. Its Plasmacoustic Metalayer™ absorbs acoustic energy directly at a surface instead of relying on conventional bulky passive absorbers or loudspeakers that cancel sound at a particular listening position.Sonexos’ initial target markets include domestic appliances, Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) and industrial systems. The company is also expanding into datacenter and energy-storage cooling, where increasingly powerful computing infrastructure is driving demand for both greater cooling capacity and effective noise management. The potential impact extends beyond acoustic performance. More compact noise-control systems can give engineers greater freedom when designing products in which space, weight and airflow are critical constraints. In applications such as data-center cooling, reducing fan noise without obstructing airflow could also help reconcile growing infrastructure needs with the interests of surrounding communities.From breakthrough technology to series production “This investment marks an important step from breakthrough technology toward industrial-scale production,” says Mark Donaldson, Founder and CEO of Sonexos. “Together with our customers and partners, we are now turning plasmacoustics into a technology that can be deployed at scale.”The investment comes at a decisive stage in Sonexos’ development. The company is already conducting paid prototype-integration programs with global manufacturers of domestic appliances and HVAC equipment. The new financing will be used primarily for industrialization, customer programs and the further development of Sonexos’ intellectual-property portfolio.The seed investment in Swiss-based Sonexos underscores Bosch Ventures’ international commitment to advancing deep-tech innovation. Complementing this international investment approach, Bosch Ventures announced its earlier this month, dedicated to investing in German deep-tech startups.

articles.title: 03.11.2026 Press release Two Wheeler EICMA 2026: Bosch is making the future of motorcycling even safer and smarter Milan, Italy – The more connected a motorcycle is, the more important it is to protect it against digital attacks. Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and cloud connections are rapidly gaining importance in the two-wheeler segment. With this in mind, and with a view to protecting vehicle electronics even more effectively, Bosch is unveiling a new, highly compact generation of its Central Gateway at EICMA 2026. For Bosch, motorcycle safety has many facets. We’re making them accessible to all riders and for every vehicle class – from accident prevention through rider-assistance systems to protecting connected vehicles against external attacks,...says Geoff Liersch, head of Two-Wheeler and Powersports at Bosch. The company is introducing this new technology specifically to help motorcycle manufacturers meet upcoming regulatory requirements: starting in December 2027, in accordance with UN Regulation R155, all newly developed two-wheeled vehicles must be secured against cyberattacks as complete systems; starting in June 2029, this requirement will also apply to all new registrations.The Central Gateway serves as a central interface to control incoming data traffic. At the trade fair, Bosch is showcasing the system in two performance classes: Light and Base. The Central Gateway Light is the company’s first highly compact 16-pin version, designed for vehicles with limited installation space, which can be integrated into existing electronic architectures with minimal effort. For premium models, the 39-pin Central Gateway Base provides additional flexibility through integrated vehicle body control functions. In addition, Bosch provides its customers a high performance Central Gateway. The 99-pin Central Gateway High is designed for future generations of vehicles with highly integrated electronic architectures. Security chips built directly into the respective control units – such as the ABS or the ECU – serve as an additional layer of protection inside the vehicle. The components are designed with cybersecurity in mind right from the factory, making it easier for vehicle manufacturers to obtain type approval in accordance with international standards. They ensure that, even in the event of external access, only verified signals reach the network. In addition, Bosch offers security services throughout the vehicle’s lifecycle such as fleet monitoring, proactive attack and intrusion detection, and vulnerability tracking during operation. “With our technology, manufacturers can meet the new global requirements while protecting riders against cyberattacks on vehicle components,” explains Geoff Liersch.Bosch presents the mobility technology of tomorrowIn addition to cybersecurity, Bosch is also continuing to advance safety and convenience on the road. When it comes to Radar-based Assistance Systems (ARAS Advanced Rider Assistance Systems), Bosch is focusing on proven technologies at EICMA: with unique features, Bosch ensures safe riding in groups or in heavy traffic. The new Triumph Tiger 1200, for example, features Bosch front and rear radar sensors to increase safety and comfort, enabling a comprehensive range of Advanced Rider Assistance Systems. This integrated package combines functions such as Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC), Group Ride Assist (GRA), and Riding Distance Assist (RDA) to increase safety and convenience while riding. Forward Collision Warning (FCW) and Blind Spot Detection (BSD) provide additional assistance by improving the rider’s awareness in all traffic situations.The display also plays a central role as the human-machine interface: Bosch’s TFT Connect System is a new generation of high-resolution instrument clusters that can be customized and connected to a smartphone. These can display not only important functions but also content such as navigation or music directly on the screen. In addition, the displays serve as a digital interface for activating functions at a later time (on-demand functions). The 7-inch version of the display is celebrating an important milestone at EICMA: the start of production in the new Triumph Tiger 1200 model.Turning to electrification, Bosch also offers a broad portfolio of powertrain systems. For smaller two-wheeled vehicles, the electric motor and inverter can be combined into a single integrated 6 kW electric drive, which makes integration easier for manufacturers. Compact electric in-hub motors provide emissions-free propulsion for e-scooters. Meanwhile, the Vehicle Control Unit (eVCU) is responsible for coordinating the entire electric powertrain. Another key focus is on a system solution for the Digital Battery Passport, which becomes a legal requirement in February 2027: this Bosch software provides motorcycle manufacturers with solutions for securely managing the required battery data throughout their vehicles’ lifecycle.
